title: माध्यमिक तहका सन्थालीभाषी विद्यार्थीहरूले नेपाली प्रयोगमा गरेका त्रुटि र तिनको निराकरणका उपाय {Errors Made by Santhali Speaking Students of Secondary Level in Using Nepali and the Ways of Their Solutions}
nepali: प्रस्तुत अध्ययन माध्यमिक तहका दोस्रोभाषी विद्यार्थीहरूले नेपालीको उच्चारण र लेखाइमा गर्ने त्रुटि र त्यसले मानक र स्तरीय नेपालीमा पार्ने प्रभावगत समस्यामा केन्द्रित रहेको छ । दोस्रोभाषी विद्यार्थीका रूपमा सन्थालीभाषालाई मातृभाषाको रूपमा प्रयोग गर्ने माध्यमिक तहमा अध्ययनरत १६ जना विद्यार्थीलाई नमुनाको रूपमा छनोट गरिएको छ । यस लेखको मुख्य उद्देश्य सन्थालीभाषी विद्यार्थीले नेपाली उच्चारण र लेखाइमा गर्ने त्रुटि पत्ता लगाई उनीहरूलाई मानक नेपाली सिकाउने उपायको खोजी गर्नु रहेको छ । यस अध्ययनमा मूलतः प्राथमिक सामग्रीलाई उपयोग गरिएको छ भने गुणात्मक र परिमाणात्मक दुवै ढाँचाको उपयोग गरिएको छ । यसमा उद्देश्यमूलक प्रक्रियाबाट अध्ययन क्षेत्र छनोट र सम्भावनायुक्त प्रक्रियाबाट नमुना छनोट गरिएको छ भने वर्णनात्मक विधिबाट तथ्याङ्कको व्याख्या र विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यस अध्ययनबाट नमुना स्वरूप दोस्रोभाषीका रूपमा छानिएका माध्यमिक तहमा अध्ययनरत सन्थालीभाषी विद्यार्थीहरूले नेपालीको उच्चारणमा भन्दा लेखाइमा बढी त्रुटिहरू गरेको देखिन्छ । विशेष गरी अजन्त, हलन्त, संयुक्त वर्ण, रेफ, ण को उच्चारण तथा लेख्य चिह्न, पदसङ्गति, पदयोग र पदवियोग जस्ता लेखाइमा त्रुटिहरू गरेको पाइन्छ । मातृभाषाको प्रभाव, भाषा सिकाइमा भएका असहजता, असावधानी र लापर्बाहीका कारण त्रुटिहरू सिर्जना भएको देखिन्छ । त्रुटि निराकरणका लागि समस्यापूर्ण क्षेत्र पहिचान गरी त्यसको कारण पत्ता लगाएर सन्थालीभाषी विद्यार्थीहरूलाई आवश्यकतानुसार मानक सामग्री तयार गरी उच्चारण गर्न लगाएर, लिखित तथा मौखिक प्रतियोगितात्मक क्रियाकलाप सञ्चालन गरेर, लिखित प्रश्नोत्तर गराएर, हौसला प्रदान गरेर, उनीहरूको आत्मविश्वास बढाएर, निरन्तर मूल्याङ्कन र अनुगमन गरी आवश्यक पृष्ठपोषण प्रदान गरेर एवम् सहकार्यात्मक अभ्यास गराएर त्रुटि न्यूनीकरण गरी मानक नेपाली भाषा सिकाउन सकिन्छ । {This study focuses on the errors made by the second language learners of the secondary level while pronouncing and writing the Nepali language, and the problems related to impact they make on the accepted and standard Nepali. Sixteen secondary level students speaking the Santhali language as their mother tongue have been selected as the sample. The main purpose of this study is to identify the errors made by the Santhali-speaking students in Nepali pronunciation and writing, and then find out the ways of teaching standard Nepali to them. In this study, only the primary sourses have been used whereas both qualitative and quantitative designs have been used. The study area has been purposively chosen and the sample randomly selected, while the data have been analyzed and interpreted using the descriptive method. From this study, it has been found that the Santhali-speaking students as second language learners studying at the secondary level selected as a sample, make more errors in writing than in the pronunciation of Nepali. Specifically, mistakes are made in writing such as ajanta, halanta, combined characters, reph, pronunciation of rna, punctuations, padasangati (word agreement), word combination and detachment (padayoga and padaviyoga). The errors seem to have been caused because of the influence of the mother tongue, discomfort of language learning, inattention and carelessness. For minimizing the errors, standard Nepali can be taught to the Santhali-speaking students by identifying the problematic areas for solving errors and finding out the reasons for them, preparing standard materials and making them pronounce as necessary, conducting writing and oral competitive activities, giving them encouragement, increasing their confidence, and providing necessary feedback by continuously evaluating and monitoring them, and involving them in collaborative practice in standard Nepali.}
american_english: This study focuses on the errors made by secondary-level second-language students in Nepali pronunciation and writing and the problems related to the impact those errors have on standard, quality Nepali. Sixteen students studying at the secondary level who use Santhali as their mother tongue have been selected as a sample of second-language students. The main purpose of this article is to identify the errors made by Santhali-speaking students in Nepali pronunciation and writing and to find ways of teaching them standard Nepali. In this study, mainly primary material has been used, and both qualitative and quantitative frameworks have been used. Here the study area has been chosen through a purposive process and the sample through a probability-based process, while data have been explained and analyzed using the descriptive method. From this study it appears that Santhali-speaking students studying at the secondary level, chosen as a sample of second-language speakers, make more errors in writing than in the pronunciation of Nepali. Specifically, errors are found in writing such as ajanta, halanta, conjunct characters, reph, the pronunciation and written sign of ṇa, padasangati, padayoga and padaviyoga. Errors appear to have been created because of the influence of the mother tongue, the discomfort in language learning, inattention and carelessness. To correct these errors, by identifying the problematic areas and finding their causes, preparing standard materials as needed and getting Santhali-speaking students to practice pronunciation, conducting written and oral competitive activities, holding written question-and-answer sessions, offering encouragement, building their self-confidence, continuously evaluating and monitoring and providing necessary feedback, and involving them in collaborative practice, the errors can be reduced and standard Nepali can be taught.

informal_english: Here's what this study's about: the mistakes secondary-level second-language students make in Nepali pronunciation and writing, and how those mistakes affect standard, quality Nepali. Sixteen secondary students who use Santhali as their mother tongue were picked as the sample. The main aim is to find the errors Santhali-speaking students make in Nepali pronunciation and writing and work out how to teach them standard Nepali. The study mainly used primary material, and both qualitative and quantitative frameworks. The study area was chosen on purpose and the sample by a probability-based process, and the data were explained and analysed using the descriptive method. What came out of it: Santhali-speaking secondary students, as second-language learners, make more errors in writing than in pronunciation. In particular, they slip up in writing on ajanta, halanta, conjunct characters, reph, the pronunciation and written sign of ṇa, padasangati, padayoga and padaviyoga. The errors seem to come from mother-tongue influence, the awkwardness of learning the language, inattention and carelessness. To fix them, you'd identify the problem areas and their causes, prepare standard materials and get students practising pronunciation, run written and oral competitions, do written Q&A, encourage them, build their confidence, keep evaluating and monitoring with feedback, and get them doing collaborative practice - that way you can cut down errors and teach standard Nepali.
